pages.title: Child Development Centers
pages.text:
# Child Development Centers

We foster physical, cognitive, social, and emotional development in a safe and nurturing environment for children ages 6 weeks to 5 years.

## Getting Started Is Easy
Offering guidance and resources to simplify child care registration.

## How to Get Started

Families seeking child care are required to submit their requests through [Military Child Care](https://public.militarychildcare.csd.disa.mil/mcc-central/mcchome) (MCC).

To initiate a request, families must first create an account with MilitaryChildCare.com, log in, and complete their household profile using the steps outlined in the link below.

[Create an Account](https://www.mcccentral.com/training-center/components/family-user-account-and-household-profile#801)

## Forms

The following forms are required for registering for child care.

Filling out pdf forms while using a government computer can be limited and recommend using a personal computer.

Please contact your local CDC with any questions, difficulties, or concerns you may have.

* [Child and Youth Programs Health Assessment](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/modules/media/?do=download&id=3490d39d-a951-4831-a364-dc3078f2b734&v=1)
* [Child and Youth Programs Registration Form](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/modules/media/?do=download&id=a20869e0-cd7e-423a-93d3-ef5fbbe59786&v=1)
* [CYP Non-Medicated Topical Products Form](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/modules/media/?do=download&id=3a6d9279-f207-4d0e-9400-1245c683da9e&v=1)
* [Application for Department of Defense Childcare Fees](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/modules/media/?do=download&id=20990cf2-e066-429b-b1f1-8de9b1782731&v=1)

Download the files and save them to a folder on your MAC or Windows computer. Make sure to open the file from the new location. If you do not have Adobe Acrobat Reader, please visit [Adobe](https://get.adobe.com/reader/) to download it for free.

## Request a Tour

Touring one of the Child Development Centers (CDCs) through Marine Corps Community Services (MCCS) can be an enlightening and heartwarming experience. Our centers are dedicated to providing quality child care and early education for your children.

Taking a tour will allow you to see the care and dedication that go into nurturing your children.

**Meet the Dedicated Staff**
The staff at the CDCs are highly trained and dedicated professionals who are passionate about early childhood education. They are committed to ensuring each child receives personalized care and attention, promoting their physical, social, emotional, and cognitive development.

**Engaging Programs**
The centers offer a variety of age-appropriate programs and activities that cater to the unique needs and interests of each child. From interactive playtime to structured learning sessions, children are encouraged to explore, discover, and learn in a fun and supportive environment.

**Safety and Security**
The safety and well-being of your children are top priority. The centers are equipped with modern security features, including secure entry points and constant supervision to ensure a safe environment for all.

**Community Focus**
Visiting a CDC also provides insight into the strong sense of community among military families. You'll witness firsthand the camaraderie and support that exist within these centers, making them more than just childcare facilities but integral parts of the military community.

**Tours are not available at all locations. Contact your local CDC to schedule a tour.**

## Child Care Resources
Providing flexible child care solutions for families.

## Full-time Child Care

**Curriculum:**

All Child Development Centers use the Early Learning Matters (ELM) curriculum as the primary classroom curriculum. ELM is based on the latest research on child development and best practices in early education and care. ELM offers a comprehensive, developmentally appropriate approach to meaningful learning for all children featuring:

* A whole child focus on skills that bolster school readiness and life success.
* Developmentally sequenced activities that embed strategies for individualizing learning.
* Evidence-informed, friendly-to-use resources for classroom staff and families.

At the heart of the ELM curriculum are activity plans that build on children's pathways of development in five infant/toddler areas and eight preschool areas. The plans support growth and development with a range of active learning opportunities that include careful attention to differences in children's abilities and interests.

**Accreditation & Certification:**

CDCs are required to be nationally accredited and must pass an annual Department of Defense inspection to obtain a certificate to operate.

## School Age Care

School Age Care (SAC) offers vital support to military families. To enroll your children into SAC, visit the [MilitaryChildCare.com](https://militarychildcare.com/).

Key Benefits:

**Safe and Structured Environment**
Provides a secure, supervised setting for children ages 5-12, ensuring peace of mind for parents during work hours and deployments.

**Academic Support**
Offers homework assistance, tutoring, and educational activities to help children excel in school and develop lifelong learning habits.

**Social Development**
Encourages children to build friendships, improve communication skills, and develop teamwork through group activities and games.

**Resilience Building**
Promotes emotional well-being and adaptability by offering programs that help children manage the unique challenges of military life, such as frequent moves and parental deployments.

**Recreational Activities**
Provides engaging, age-appropriate recreational activities that promote physical fitness, creativity, and exploration.

**Support for Military Readiness**
Enables military parents to focus on their mission, knowing their children are in a supportive, enriching environment.

**Affordable and Flexible Care Options**
Offers cost-effective programs tailored to the needs of military families, with flexible care schedules to accommodate varying work hours.

**Connection to MCCS Resources**
Provides access to other MCCS programs, such as Family Advocacy, Youth Sports, and the Exceptional Family Member Program (EFMP), ensuring comprehensive support for families.

School Age Care programs are designed to strengthen military families and help children thrive, fostering a sense of community and stability within the Marine Corps lifestyle.

## Hourly Child Care

Hourly child care may be available on your installation Child Development Centers (CDC) for an hourly rate per child.

* Hourly child care does not require parents to make a request on [militarychildcare.com](https://militarychildcare.com/).
* Parents need to complete and submit the CDC packet and provide the necessary supporting documents to register their child.
* This service is provided based on space availability or may not be offered at your installation.
* Contact your local installation's CDC for availability.

## Family Support Resources
Connecting families to essential tools and resources.

## PCS Workshop

The Permanent Change of Station (PCS) Workshop is designed to guide Marines and their families through every step of the relocation process. Whether it's your first move or one of many, our workshop provides valuable insights and resources to help you transition with ease.

Nine reasons to attend a PCS Workshop:

1. **Policy**
Per MCO 1754.10B, attending the PCS Workshop is required for a smooth transition to your new duty station.

2. **Installation-specific Information and Contacts**
Get valuable information about your new installation, including key contacts and local services.

3. **Household Goods Weight Allowances & Entitlements**
Learn about your weight allowances for household goods and what entitlements you can access during your move.

4. **Travel Allowances, Budget, and Government Card**
Understand your travel allowances, how to budget for the move, and how to use your government travel card.

5. **Moving with Pets**
Receive guidance on transporting pets, quarantine regulations, and other related requirements.

6. **School Liaison & Exceptional Family Member Program Resources**
Access support for school enrollment and resources for family members with special needs.

7. **Spouse Employment Opportunities**
Discover job search assistance and career development resources for spouses.

8. **Personalized Relocation Plan & Online Relocation Resources**
Create a customized relocation plan and explore online resources to streamline your move.

9. **Sponsorship**
As per MCO 1320.11H, learn how to request a sponsor to help you adjust and settle into your new duty station.

Don't move alone. Contact your [Information, Referral, and Relocation](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/information-referral-and-relocation) specialist for PCS Workshop information.

## School Liaison

The School Liaison is a vital resource for Marines and their families new to an installation, helping to ensure a seamless transition for children into local schools. By providing essential information and support, the School Liaison assists families in navigating educational options and addressing any concerns related to their child's education.

School Liaison support includes:

* **School Enrollment**
Guidance on enrolling children in local schools and understanding registration requirements.

* **Local School Information**
Up-to-date resources about school districts, programs, and options available in the area.

* **Home School Information**
Assisting families with guidance on registering with the DoDEA schools.

* **Exceptional Family Member Support**
Help with navigating the special education process and accessing available services.

* **Transition Assistance**
Resources for families moving to a new area, including information on school calendars and schedules.

These services help ensure that children receive the support they need for a successful educational experience in their new community.

For more information about support and services, visit the [School Liaison](https://yuma.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/child-and-youth/school-liaison) webpage on the MCCS website.

## Exceptional Family Member Program

The Exceptional Family Member Program (EFMP) is essential for service members and their families with special needs, providing support and resources to ensure a smooth transition to a new installation.

EFMP helps families navigate the challenges associated with relocating by connecting them to specialized services and community resources tailored to their unique circumstances.

EFMP Services Available Include:

* **Enrollment Assistance**
Guidance on enrolling in the EFMP and understanding program requirements.

* **Specialized Support Services**
Access to resources for medical, educational, and emotional support tailored to family members with special needs.

* **Transition Assistance**
Help with relocating to a new area, including information on local schools, medical facilities, and community services.

* **Advocacy and Resources**
Connection to advocacy services and local support groups to assist families in accessing necessary care and benefits.

* **Workshops and Training**
Opportunities for families to participate in workshops focused on managing special needs and navigating available resources.

Learn more about how EFMP supports you and your family by visiting [EFMP](https://usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/military-family-life/exceptional-family-member-program).

## Marine Corps Family Team Building

Eligibility for participation in the Marine Corps Family Team Building (MCFTB) programs extend to individuals across various segments of the military community. This includes:

* Active Duty Service Members: Including all branches of the military, all ranks.
* Department of Defense (DoD) Employees
* Spouses of Military Personnel

MCFTB is designed to enhance the resilience, readiness, and well-being of all members of the Marine Corps community, including service members, spouses, children, extended family members, command leaders, units, and support personnel.

**How to get started with MCFTB:**

1. **Identify Individual Needs:** Determine what specific support or resources you or your family require. MCFTB offers a variety of workshops, classes, and resources tailored to different needs, including deployment support, spouse education and career assistance, relationship-enhancement, and more.

MCFTB professionals can help you identify your specific needs.

2. **Connect with MCFTB:** Reach out to MCFTB professionals either in person or by phone. They can provide guidance on available programs, workshops, and resources that best suit your needs.

3. **Attend Workshops and Classes:** Participate in MCFTB workshops, classes, and events relevant to your situation. These could include pre-deployment briefs, relationship-enhancement classes, pre-marital and marital workshops, relocation assistance workshops, family readiness seminars, financial planning classes, and more.

4. **Connect with Other Families:** Take advantage of opportunities to connect with other Marine Corps families through MCFTB-sponsored events, support groups, and social media platforms. Building connections with other families can provide valuable support and camaraderie.

## New Parent Support

New Parent Support offers guidance, education, and support to our Marines, their families throughout our military community. Eligible participants can access resources provided by New Parent Support.

Eligible Participants:

* Parents with children up to age 5
* DoD Spouses
* DoD Families

Connect with your New Parent Support office to begin your journey with our caring professionals.

## Information, Referral, and Relocation

**Information, Referral, and Relocation (IR&R) services** to support Marines and their families through life's transitions, whether it's a Permanent Change of Station (PCS), deployment, or other major milestones. These services are designed to ease the challenges of relocation and connect families to valuable resources within their community.

### **Key Services Provided:**

* **Welcome Aboard Brief**
Provides newcomers with essential information about their new installation, local community, and available resources.

* **Relocation Assistance**
Offers one-on-one support for PCS moves, including help with planning, moving tips, and checklists to ensure a smooth transition.

* **Requesting a Sponsor**
Connects Marines and their families with trained sponsors to provide personalized support and guidance during relocation.

* **Lending Locker**
Supplies temporary household items, such as kitchenware and small appliances, to help families settle in while awaiting their belongings.

* **Base Housing Support**
Offers guidance on housing options, including on-base housing, rental listings, and off-base accommodations.

* **DEERS and ID Card Assistance**
Provides information and support for enrolling in the Defense Enrollment Eligibility Reporting System (DEERS) and obtaining necessary ID cards.

* **Child Care and School Liaison Support**
Helps families find child care and connects them with School Liaison Officers for school registration and educational resources.

* **Exceptional Family Member Program (EFMP) Support**
Ensures families with special needs have access to tailored relocation assistance and resources at their new duty station.

### **Benefits of IR&R Services**

* Reduces stress and uncertainty associated with frequent moves.
* Enhances readiness by ensuring families are well-informed and prepared.
* Strengthens connections within the Marine Corps community.
* Provides access to resources that promote resilience and stability.

Whether you're transitioning to a new duty station or looking for local resources, IR&R services are here to support you every step of the way.

## Life Skill-building Resources
Developing skills for personal and professional growth.

## Budgeting for Child Care

The professionals at [Personal Financial Management](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/personal-financial-management) can help you prepare for financial changes by offering guidance on budgeting, saving, and managing child care expenses.

## Managing Stress

The Community Counseling Program utilizes a holistic approach to support individuals, children, couples, and families. Our professional clinicians provide solutions designed to meet your specific needs in the following areas:

* Relationship Concerns
* Work Stressors
* Life Stressors

Establish a connection with professionals from your Community Counseling center and discover a successful journey toward overcoming life's challenges.

[Community Counseling](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/prevention-and-counseling/community-counseling)

## Frequently Asked Question (FAQs)
### What ages does the Child Development Center serve?

The Child Development Center provides child care to children from 6 weeks to 5 years old.

### How do I enroll my child in the Child Development Centers?

Enrollment is completed through [MilitaryChildCare.com](https://militarychildcare.com/), where you can create an account, select your preferences, and join the waitlist.

### What types of activities does the Child Development Center offer?

The Child Development Center provides age-appropriate activities that promote cognitive, social, emotional, and physical development through a structured curriculum.

# Family Child Care

We provide your child, aged 6 weeks to 12 years, with a nurturing environment, that supports their development and helps them thrive within the community.

## Getting Started is Easy
Navigating steps to successfully register for child care.

## Registration Guidance
Welcome to Family Child Care (FCC), where your child will learn, grow, and thrive in a safe and supportive environment. FCC Providers are highly trained and regulated, including thorough background checks and monthly inspections. FCC providers create a sense of belonging for families and support them in developing their child(ren)'s positive self-worth. We're excited to be part of your community.

Registration is quick and easy—simply follow the steps below.

1. **Go to** [MilitaryChildCare.com](https://militarychildcare.com/).
   - Set up an account if you don't already have one.
   - Add your child's information and request care at your installation.

2. **Join the Waitlist**
   - If space is not immediately available, your child will be placed on a waitlist.
   - You will receive an offer via email to inform you when a spot opens up.
   - If you are placed on a waitlist you have the option of contacting [MCCYN](https://public.militarychildcare.csd.disa.mil/mcc-central/mcchome/mccyn) which provides fee assistance to offset the costs of community-based care.

3. **Accept the Offer**
   - Once you receive an offer, follow the instructions to accept it within the given timeframe.
   - If you don't respond within the timeframe, the offer is removed, but you may request reactivation with supporting details if eligible.

4. **Complete the Registration Process**
   - After accepting the offer, you will receive forms to complete.
   - Provide necessary documents, such as proof of eligibility, immunization records, and emergency contacts.

5. **Attend Parent Orientation**
   - You will be required to attend an orientation to review program policies and expectations.

6. **Start Care**
   - Once all paperwork is submitted and fees are processed, your child can begin attending the program.

If you need help getting started please contact our Resource and Referral office. They can answer questions and guide you through the process.

## Eligibility
Family Child Care (FCC) provides a safe, enriching environment for children while supporting the unique needs of military families. We proudly serve those who serve by offering quality care that fosters learning, resilience, and connection. FCC providers establish their own schedules and may provide care outside standard work hours.

**Family Child Care is available to children of:**

- Active-duty Service Members
- DoD Civilian Employees
- Reservists
- DoD contractors.

**Children:**

- Must be between the ages of 6 weeks to 12 years old.

**Enrollment:**

- Enrollment is guided by DoD priorities. Supplanting does not apply to FCC. To secure a spot, families are encouraged to register early, as availability may vary depending on demand.

**Department of Defense Policies:**

- [DoDI 6060.02](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/modules/media/?do=download&id=c8ad90d5-2d16-44a7-95b6-224de21dfd54&v=1)
- [MCO 1710.30A](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/modules/media/?do=download&id=a98aa33f-1d48-4466-8530-c790d725bfed&v=1)

For more information on eligibility, priority placement, and registration requirements, please contact our Resource and Referral office.

## MilitaryChildCare.com
MilitaryChildCare.com makes it easy to find and request Family Child Care (FCC), giving you peace of mind knowing your child is in a safe and supportive environment.

With just one online account, you can explore program options, submit a request, and manage your childcare needs from anywhere. Spaces are assigned based on DoD priority placement, so registering early ensures you have the best chance of securing care when you need it.

Start today by visiting [MilitaryChildCare.com](https://public.militarychildcare.csd.disa.mil/mcc-central/mcchome).

## Child Care Support
Exploring child care opportunities.

## I Need Child Care
Family Child Care is a great child care choice offered right in your community. Certified providers care for small groups of children in their own homes, either on the installation or nearby. Think of it as quality child care in a comfortable, home-like setting.

**Flexible, Home-Based Child Care for Your Family**

Family Child Care (FCC) offers a safe, nurturing, and home-like environment for children ages 6 weeks to 12 years. With small group sizes and flexible hours, FCC provides personalized care that fits your family's schedule, including full-time, part-time, evening, and weekend options. Licensed providers are trained to support your child's development while ensuring a warm, engaging atmosphere.

**Eligibility & Requirements:**

Family Child Care (FCC) is designed to support military families by providing high-quality, home-based child care. Eligibility is based on priority and availability.

- Active-Duty Service Members
- Department of Defense (DoD) Civilians
- Reservists & National Guard Members
- Retirees
- DoD Contractors

To ensure a safe and developmentally appropriate environment, children enrolled in the Family Child Care (FCC) program must meet the following requirements:

**Age Requirements**

- Children must be between 6 weeks and 12 years old to enroll in FCC.
- School-age children (up to 12 years) may attend before/after school care, full-day care during school breaks, and summer programs.

**Health & Immunization Requirements**

- All children must have up-to-date immunization records, including age-appropriate vaccines as required by DoD and state regulations.

**Special Needs & Accommodations**

- The CYP behavior specialist, CYP nurse, and FCC providers work together to assess and accommodate children with special needs.
- Parents must disclose any medical, developmental, or dietary requirements during registration to ensure proper care and support.

If you have any question please contact our Resource and Referral office.

## I Want to Provide Child Care
As an Family Child Care provider, you'll offer safe, high-quality care for military children while enjoying flexible hours, professional training, and the ability to care for your own children at home. MCCS provides free training, support, and resources to help you succeed.

Start your journey today—make a difference in the lives of military families while building your own career! Contact your local Family Child Care office to learn more.

**Why Become an FCC Provider?**

- Run your own home-based business while supporting military families.
- Enjoy flexible hours and the ability to care for your own children at home.
- Receive training and support at no cost, including CPR, First Aid, and child development courses.
- Gain access to resources and equipment, including a lending library of toys and materials.
- Participate in the USDA Child and Adult Care Food Program to receive meal reimbursements.

**Eligibility Requirements:**

- Must be at least 18 years old.
- Have a high school diploma or equivalent.
- Reside in government housing or approved off-base housing.
- Pass a comprehensive background check for all household members over 18.
- Complete a health screening for yourself and any family members who will be in the home.

**Steps to Get Started:**

1. Contact your local Family Child Care office to learn more about the application process and training requirements.
2. Download and complete the FCC Application or obtain it from the Resource and Referral office. Applicaton requires background checks.
3. Complete a family interview (provider applicant and spouse)
4. If interested in processing with the certification process, background checks are initiated.
5. Pay a non-refundable $50 training fee at Family Child Care office which covers the cost of the CPR/First Aid training. _Training fees are not required at all locations. Contact the Resource and Referral office about training fees._
6. Attend FCC Provider initial training - 40-hours (one-week)
7. Complete health requirements for all household members,
8. Set up home in accordance with regulatory requirements.
9. Home inspection by Fire, Safety & Sanitation.
10. Quality Review Board.
11. Documentation sent to SJA regarding successfully completion of requirements (to obtain authorization to operate a home business).
12. (Upon SJA approval) Provider files Housing Addendum, notifying Family Housing of FCC business
13. Purchase Liability Insurance.
14. Upon clearance to start, Resource & Referral will assist in setting up provider's profile on [MilitaryChildCare.com](https://militarychildcare.com/)
15. Final walk-through by FCC staff.
16. Open for business!
17. Be committed to attending ongoing training sessions to guarantee the highest quality of care for children. This includes monthly evening training.

Homes should obtain certification from the command if they provide more than 10 "child care hours" per week. For instance, if a resident looks after two children for five hours, it amounts to 10 hours of child care. Homes that operate outside this framework without certification will be deemed unauthorized. Enforcement against such unauthorized care will be as per the Housing Office rules and regulations. Detailed information can be found on page 6 of the Resident handbook.

The FCC program is not only about providing care but also about ensuring that the caregivers are well-trained, certified, and provide a safe and nurturing environment for the children. The command plays an active role in monitoring and certifying providers, ensuring the best care for the children enrolled in the FCC program.

If you have any questions please contact our Resource and Referral office.

## Life Skill-building Resources
Developing essential skills for personal and professional growth.

## School Liaison
The School Liaison is a vital resource for Marines and their families new to an installation, helping to ensure a seamless transition for children into local schools. By providing essential information and support, the School Liaison assists families in navigating educational options and addressing any concerns related to their child's education.

School Liaison support include:

- **School Enrollment** Guidance on enrolling children in local schools and understanding registration requirements.
- **Local School Information** Up-to-date resources about school districts, programs, and options available in the area.
- **Home School Information** Assisting families with guidance on their local school district homeschool requirements.
- **Special Education Support** Help with navigating the special education process and accessing available services to include warm hand offs to EFMP.
- **Transition Assistance** Resources for families moving to a new area, including information on school calendars and schedules.

These services help ensure that children receive the support they need for a successful educational experience in their new community.

For more information about support and services, visit the [School Liaison](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/child-and-youth/school-liaison) webpage on the MCCS website.

## Exceptional Family Member Program
The Exceptional Family Member Program (EFMP) is essential for service members and their families with special needs, providing support and resources to ensure a smooth transition to a new installation.

EFMP helps families navigate the challenges associated with relocating by connecting them to specialized services and community resources tailored to their unique circumstances.

EFMP Services Available Include:

- **Enrollment Assistance** Guidance on enrolling in the EFMP and understanding program requirements.
- **Specialized Support Services** Access to resources for medical, educational, and emotional support tailored to family members with special needs.
- **Transition Assistance** Help with relocating to a new area, including information on local schools, medical facilities, and community services.
- **Advocacy and Resources** Connection to advocacy services and local support groups to assist families in accessing necessary care and benefits.
- **Workshops and Training** Opportunities for families to participate in workshops focused on managing special needs and navigating available resources.

Learn more about how EFMP supports you and your family by visiting [EFMP](https://usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/military-family-life/exceptional-family-member-program).

## Budgeting Your Child Care
The professionals at [Personal Financial Management](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/personal-financial-management) can help you prepare for financial changes by offering guidance on budgeting, saving, and managing educational expenses.

**Life Skills Development Resources:**

- Blended Retirement System (BRS)
- Car Buying
- Consumer Awareness
- Continuation Pay
- Couple Financial Counseling
- Credit Report and Credit Score Analysis Saving and Investing
- Credit / Debt Management
- Developing a Spending Plan
- Financial Education Action Points (FEAP)
- Individual Financial Counseling
- Major Purchases
- Military Pay & Benefits
- Retirement Planning
- Survivor Benefits Plan
- Thrift Savings Plan
- Understanding Military Retirement Benefits

## Marine Corps Family Team Building
[Marine Corps Family Team Building](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/military-family-life/marine-corps-family-team-building) (MCFTB) is designed to enhance the resilience, readiness, and well-being of all members of the Marine Corps community, including service members, spouses, children, extended family members, command leaders, units, and support personnel.

How to get started with MCFTB:

- **Identify Individual Needs** Determine what specific support or resources you or your family require. MCFTB offers a variety of workshops, classes, and resources tailored to different needs, including deployment support, spouse education and career assistance, relationship-enhancement, and more. MCFTB professionals can help you identify your specific needs.
- **Connect with MCFTB** Reach out to MCFTB professionals either in person or by phone. They can provide guidance on available programs, workshops, and resources that best suit your needs.
- **Attend Workshops and Classes** Participate in MCFTB workshops, classes, and events relevant to your situation. These could include pre-deployment briefs, relationship-enhancement classes, pre-marital and marital workshops, relocation assistance workshops, family readiness seminars, financial planning classes, and more.
- **Connect with Other Families** Take advantage of opportunities to connect with other Marine Corps families through MCFTB-sponsored events, support groups, and social media platforms. Building connections with other families can provide valuable support and camaraderie.

## Libraries
The [Library](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/libraries) is a great resource for families and school-age children, offering books, educational programs, and activities that support learning and growth. Whether you're looking for homework help, fun storytimes, or a quiet place to read and explore, the Library provides a welcoming space for children to develop their love of learning. Stop by and discover all the ways we support your family!

**Life Skills Development Resources:**

- **Children's Collection:** A diverse selection of picture books, chapter books, movies, and audiobooks designed for young readers.
- **Summer Reading Program:** Featuring free activities and incentives to encourage a love of reading during the summer months.
- **Storytime Kits:** Themed kits that include books and activities, allowing families to enjoy storytime at their convenience.
- **Educational Programs and Activities:** Various events and workshops that enrich your children's learning experiences.
- **Access to Digital Resources:** Online materials, including e-books and educational databases, to support learning and exploration. Visit the [DoD MWR Virtual Library](https://marines.dodmwrlibraries.org./).

## Guiding Growth & Resilience
[Community Counseling](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/prevention-and-counseling/community-counseling) provides support to ease this transition by offering emotional support, stress management strategies, and adjustment counseling. Counselors help families navigate the challenges of relocation, offering guidance on coping with change, building resilience, and connecting with local resources.

Through individual and family counseling, the program helps create a smooth transition, strengthening the overall well-being of military families.

- Life Skills Development Resources:
- Relationship Concerns
- Work Stressors
- Life Stressors
- Trauma
- EAS/PCS and Challenges Related to Transition
- Grief and Loss
- Sadness
- Worry
- Deployment Cycle Stressors and Reintegration
- Adjustment
- Crisis Intervention
- Sleep Hygiene
- Parent-Child Communication

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)
**Who can become a Family Child Care provider?**

Any military spouse or eligible individual 18 years or older who lives in base housing or approved off-base housing can apply. Providers must complete training, background checks, and home inspections to become licensed.

**What are the benefits of becoming an FCC provider?**

FCC providers run their own home-based business, set their own hours, care for their own children while earning income, receive free training and resources, and participate in the USDA Child and Adult Care Food Program.

**What are the requirements for enrolling a child in FCC?**

Children must be between 6 weeks and 12 years old, have up-to-date immunizations, and meet health and safety requirements. Families must register through MilitaryChildCare.com or their local Resource & Referral (R&R) office.

**How is Family Child Care different from a Child Development Center (CDC)?**

FCC provides home-based care in smaller groups, offering more personalized attention, flexible hours, and a family-like setting compared to larger Child Development Centers (CDCs).

**How do I find an FCC provider for my child?**

Parents can search for available FCC providers and request care through MilitaryChildCare.com or contact their local FCC office or Resource & Referral (R&R) office for assistance.

Contact: Family Child Care
Address: Marine Corps Community Services
Contact your local Resource and Referral office for assistance

# New Parent Support

The New Parent Support Program (NPSP) is a voluntary strength-based parent education program which is delivered through education and support, parent support groups, and the ability to link parents to appropriate referrals and resources. Program eligibility is offered to all service members, family members who are expectant parents, and parents of children from birth to five years of age.

Even if you have been raising your family for a few years, challenges may arise as your child grows and develops. The NPSP offers you the opportunity to express your concerns, ask questions, enhance parent child relationships and parenting techniques, build skills, set goals, and gain new knowledge. Please contact us for more information at [(703) 784-4248](tel:7037844248).

## Baby Boot Camp
Learn how to make the time you have with your baby as stress-free and enjoyable as possible. Learn coping skills to decrease anxiety of first time parenting. Learn the basics of newborn care. Learn how to calm a fussy baby and reduce the risk of Shaken Baby Syndrome.

## Pregnancy 101
Explore pregnancy, labor, and delivery. Gaining knowledge and asking questions early can reduce stress and support your pregnancy journey.

## Mothers In Formation
Mothers In Formation is a supportive space for active duty moms to connect, share experiences, and build community. This monthly group offers encouragement, stress-management tools, and discussion around balancing military life and motherhood. Join us to connect with other moms, strengthen support networks, and focus on your well-being.

## Post-Partum Support International
The purpose of the organization is to increase awareness among public and professional communities about the emotional changes that women experience during pregnancy and postpartum. Approximately 15% of all women will experience postpartum depression following the birth of a child. Up to 10% will experience depression or anxiety during pregnancy. When the mental health of the mother is compromised, it affects the entire family.

[https://www.postpartum.net/](https://www.postpartum.net/)

## Breastfeeding Basics
Class Focus: Breastfeeding

## Home Visitation
**What is Home Visitation?**

The New Parent Support Program Home Visitors are Licensed Clinicians, Licensed Social Workers and/or Licensed Marriage Family Therapists. The purpose of home visits is to provide individualized parenting education and support to parents of young children up to age six and to help parents increase their parenting skills so that they are successful parenting their children throughout each stage of development. Home visits take place in the family's home. The frequency of the visits range from once a week to once a month depending on your family's needs and interests.

Home Visitors provide education on a variety of topics to include, but not limited to: age appropriate discipline, developmental screenings, managing sibling rivalry, effective communication with your children, stress management, toilet training, nutrition, Sudden Infant Death Syndrome and deployment issues.

Some people receive parenting education, while others request support and encouragement regarding the challenges of parenting.

Call [(703) 784-4248](tel:7037844248) to register.

# School Age Care

We offer a safe, engaging environment for children ages 5-12, providing homework assistance, recreational activities, and social development opportunities to support their growth and well-being.

## Getting Started is Easy
Learn about eligibility and registration.

Enrolling your child in School Age Care is simple.

Welcome to School Age Care (SAC), where your child will learn, grow, and thrive in a safe and supportive environment. Through engaging activities, meaningful connections, and opportunities to build essential life skills, SAC supports children to develop confidence, resilience, and a sense of belonging. We're excited to be part of their journey!

Registration is quick and easy—simply follow the steps below.

1. **Go to** [MilitaryChildCare.com](https://militarychildcare.com/).
   - Set up an account if you don't already have one.
   - Add your child's information and request care at your installation.

2. **Join the Waitlist**
   - If space is not immediately available, your child will be placed on a waitlist.
   - You will receive an offer when a spot opens up.
   - If you are placed on a waitlist you have the option of contacting [MCCYN](https://public.militarychildcare.csd.disa.mil/mcc-central/mcchome/mccyn) which provides fee assistance to offset the costs of community-based care.

3. **Accept the Offer**
   - Once you receive an offer, follow the instructions to accept it within the given timeframe.
   - If you don't respond within the timeframe, the offer is removed, but you may request reactivation with supporting details if eligible.

4. **Complete the Registration Process**
   - After accepting the offer, you will receive forms to complete.
   - Provide necessary documents, such as proof of eligibility, Flu shot records, and emergency contacts.

5. **Attend Parent Orientation**
   - You may be required to attend an orientation to review program policies and expectations.

6. **Start Care**
   - Once all paperwork is submitted and fees are processed, your child can begin attending the program.

If you need help, contact the Resource and Referral office. They can answer questions and guide you through the process.

## Eligibility
Exploring the requirements and determining if you qualify.

School Age Care (SAC) is designed to provide a safe, enriching environment for children while supporting the unique needs of military families. We proudly serve those who serve by offering quality care that fosters learning, resilience, and connection.

**School Age Care is available to children of:**

- Active-duty Service Members
- DoD Civilian Employees
- Reservists
- DoD contractors.

**Children:**

- Must be between the ages of 5 and 12 years old
- Enrolled in Kindergarten through 6th grade to participate in the program.

**Enrollment:**

- Enrollment is guided by DoD priorities. To secure a spot, families are encouraged to register early, as availability may vary depending on demand.

**Department of Defense Policies:**

- [DoDI 6060.02](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/modules/media/?do=download&id=c8ad90d5-2d16-44a7-95b6-224de21dfd54&v=1)
- [MCO 1710.30A](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/modules/media/?do=download&id=a98aa33f-1d48-4466-8530-c790d725bfed&v=1)

For more information on eligibility, priority placement, and registration requirements, contact the Resource and Referral office.

## MilitaryChildCare.com
Registering online is easy and convenient.

MilitaryChildCare.com makes it easy to find and request School Age Care (SAC), giving you peace of mind knowing your child is in a safe and supportive environment.

With just one online account, you can explore program options, submit a request, and manage your childcare needs from anywhere. Spaces are offered based on DoD priority placement.

Start today by visiting [MilitaryChildCare.com](https://public.militarychildcare.csd.disa.mil/mcc-central/mcchome).

## School Age Care Support
Providing child care for the military community.

## Curriculum Focus
Supporting your child's growth and development.

School Age Care (SAC) is designed to provide a safe, engaging, and enriching environment that helps children grow academically, socially, and emotionally. Our curriculum is built around key focus areas that promote well-rounded development:

- **Character & Leadership Development**
  Encouraging responsibility, teamwork, and leadership skills to help children build confidence and a sense of community.

- **Education & Career Development**
  Providing opportunities for hands-on learning, homework support, and activities that spark curiosity and future career interests.

- **Health & Life Skills**
  Teaching the importance of healthy habits, personal responsibility, and essential life skills to promote long-term well-being.

- **The Arts**
  Fostering creativity and self-expression through music, dance, visual arts, and drama.

- **Sports, Fitness & Recreation**
  Promoting physical activity and teamwork through structured sports and recreational games.

- **Technology**
  Offering STEM-based activities that introduce children to coding, robotics, and problem-solving in a fun, interactive way.

Our program follows nationally recognized standards and is affiliated with the Boys & Girls Clubs of America (BGCA) to ensure high-quality experiences that support the overall well-being of children.

By participating in the School Age Care, your child will gain valuable skills, make lasting friendships, and enjoy a supportive environment that helps them thrive.

If you have any questions about the curriculum please contact the Resource and Referral office.

## Meals Provided
Nutritious options to fuel your child's play.

School Age Care (SAC) ensures your child will enjoy balanced, nutritious meals and snacks that keep them energized and ready to learn, play, and grow. We provide wholesome options that support their overall health and development, ensuring they stay energized throughout the day.

What's Included?

- **Before & After School Care**
  A nutritious breakfast and an afternoon snack are provided.

- **Early Release / Teacher Workdays / School Breaks**
  Breakfast, lunch, and an afternoon snack are included.

**Special Dietary Needs**
Inform School Age Care staff of any food allergies or dietary requirements during registration. We will work with you to accommodate where possible.

**Encouraging Healthy Eating**
Our meals follow USDA nutritional guidelines, ensuring a well-balanced diet with a focus on fruits, vegetables, whole grains, and protein. We encourage healthy eating habits and teach children the importance of making good food choices.

Meals offered can vary by location, check with the School Age Care center for details.

[USDA Non-Discrimination Statement](https://www.usda.gov/non-discrimination-statement)

For more information about meals offered and dietary accommodation requirements, please contact the Resource and Referral office.

## Transportation
Safe and reliable travel for your child.

School Age Care (SAC) provides safe and dependable transportation to help your child get to and from care with ease. Our goal is to ensure a smooth transition between school and our center, giving you peace of mind while supporting your child's daily routine.

What's Included?

- **On-Base Schools**
  Transportation is typically provided for children attending schools located on the installation.

- **Off-Base Schools**
  Availability of transportation for off-base schools varies by location. Please check with your local center for details.

- **Field Trips & Special Activities**
  During school breaks and summer camp, supervised transportation is provided for planned excursions and enrichment activities.

**Parent Responsibilities**
If your child attends a school that is not part of the SAC transportation service, you will need to arrange their drop-off and pick-up.

**Safety First**
Our transportation services follow strict safety guidelines, and all vehicles are operated by trained professionals. Children are supervised at all times during transit to ensure their safety and well-being.

Not all installations provide transportation. For more information on transportation options at your location, contact the Resource and Referral office.

## Youth Connections
Helping your child feel at home.

Youth Connections is designed to help children adjust, make friends, and feel comfortable in their new community. Whether your family is new to the installation or transitioning from another program, we ensure your child feels welcome and supported from day one at School Age Care (SAC).

How it works:

- **Peer Support**
  When a new child joins the program, they are paired with a friendly and experienced SAC ambassador—a peer who helps them navigate their new environment.

- **Guided Introductions**
  The ambassador introduces them to other children, explains daily routines, and helps them feel included in activities.

- **Building Connections**
  Through shared activities, games, and team projects, new children quickly become part of the SAC community.

Why It Matters

- **Reduces Anxiety**
  Having a familiar face and a peer to guide them makes the transition easier and less overwhelming.

- **Encourages Friendships**
  Children develop friendships faster when they have someone to introduce them to others.

- **Promotes Leadership**
  SAC ambassadors take pride in their role, learning valuable leadership and mentoring skills.

Becoming a SAC Ambassador

- Children who have been in the program for a while and show leadership, kindness, and responsibility may be invited to become an ambassador.

- SAC ambassadors receive guidance on how to support new peers and foster a welcoming environment.

- Youth Connection helps children feel confident, connected, and ready to enjoy their time in School Age Care.

If your child is new or interested in becoming part of Youth Connections, talk to the SAC team to learn more!

## Parent Orientation
Setting you and your child up for success.

Parent Orientation is an essential step in ensuring a smooth and positive experience for both you and your child in School Age Care (SAC). An orientation provides important information about program policies, daily routines, and what to expect, helping you feel confident and informed from day one.

What to Expect in Parent Orientation
During the orientation, you will:

- **Learn About Program Policies & Expectations**
  Review SAC guidelines on pick-up and drop-off procedures, behavior expectations, and communication with staff.

- **Understand Safety & Emergency Procedures**
  Learn how SAC ensures your child's safety, including emergency plans, health protocols, and supervision standards.

- **Review Meals & Nutrition**
  Get details about meal schedules, snack options, and dietary restrictions or allergies.

- **Meet SAC Staff & Ask Questions**
  Connect with the SAC professionals, program directors, and support staff who will be working with your child every day.

- **Complete Required Paperwork**
  Ensure all necessary forms, including medical information and emergency contacts, are finalized before your child starts care.

**Why Parent Orientation is Important**

- Helps you understand how the program operates and what is expected of both parents and children.
- Gives you a chance to meet the staff and ask any questions before your child's first day.
- Ensures a smooth transition, setting your child up for success in the SAC environment.

Attending Parent Orientation is the best way to get familiar with the program and feel confident that your child is in a safe, structured, and supportive environment.

If you have any questions or need to schedule your orientation, please contact the Resource and Referral office.

## Supporting Children with Special Needs
Striving to offer the best possible care and accommodations.

School Age Care (SAC) is committed to providing an supportive and enriching environment for all children. We recognize that every child has unique needs, and we strive to offer the best possible care and accommodations to ensure their success.

**How We Support**

- We work closely with families to understand each child's specific needs. Individualized support plans are developed to ensure appropriate accommodations.

**Trained & Caring Staff**

- Our staff members receive specialized training on working with children with various needs, including strategies for positive behavior support, communication techniques, and safety protocols.
- We collaborate with the family, SAC nurses, and SAC behavior specialists to provide the best care possible.

**Adaptive Activities & Programming**

- Activities are adapted, allowing all children to participate in a way that meets their needs.
- We foster a welcoming environment where all children feel valued and included.

**Facility Accessibility & Safety Measures**

- SAC facilities are designed to accommodate children with physical, sensory, or developmental challenges.
- Emergency preparedness plans consider the needs of all children, ensuring a safe environment.

**Ongoing Communication & Family Collaboration**

- School Age Care professionals communicate directly with parents to ensure the best experience for their child.
- Adjustments and accommodations can be made as needed to support each child's development and well-being.

**How to Request Accommodations**

- During the registration process, inform SAC staff that your child has special needs.
- Complete required Child & Youth documentations.
- Provide relevant documentation or recommendations from medical providers, or therapists if applicable.
- Work with SAC staff to develop a support plan that best supports your child's needs.

At School Age Care, we provide a high-quality that promotes positive outcomes in all areas of children's development, every child can thrive. If your child has special needs and you have questions about accommodations, contact the Resource and Referral office. We are here to support you!

## Seasonal Camps
Explore, learn, and grow with engaging activities that inspire confidence, creativity, and connection.

Seasonal camps provide a safe, engaging environment where children ages 5-12 can explore new interests, build friendships, and develop essential life skills. Through fun activities, hands-on learning, and supportive guidance, our camps foster confidence, resilience, and a strong sense of community. Whether through sports, creative arts, STEM projects, or outdoor adventures, children stay active, inspired, and ready to grow.

View the upcoming camps listed in our calendar or contact the Resource and Referral office.

## School Liaison
Providing essential information and support for a positive academic experience for your children.

The School Liaison is a vital resource for Marines and their families. By providing essential information and support, the School Liaison assists families in navigating educational options and addressing any concerns related to their child's education.

School Liaison support include:

- **School Enrollment**
  Guidance on enrolling children in local schools and understanding registration requirements.

- **Local School Information**
  Up-to-date resources about school districts, programs, and options available in the area.

- **Home School Information**
  Assisting families with guidance on their local school district homeschool requirements.

- **Special Education Support**
  Help with navigating the special education process and accessing available services to include warm hand offs to EFMP.

- **Transition Assistance**
  Resources for families moving to a new area, including information on school calendars and schedules.

These services help ensure that children receive the support they need for a successful educational experience in their new community.

For more information about support and services, visit the [School Liaison](https://yuma.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/child-and-youth/school-liaison).

## Life Skill-building Resources
Learn additional life skills that support you and your family.

## Guiding Growth & Resilience
Helping children thrive through guidance and support.

[Community Counseling](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/prevention-and-counseling/community-counseling) provides support to ease this transition by offering emotional support, stress management strategies, and adjustment counseling. Counselors help families navigate the challenges of relocation, offering guidance on coping with change, building resilience, and connecting with local resources.

Through individual and family counseling, the program helps create a smooth transition, strengthening the overall well-being of military families.

- Life Skills Development Resources:
- Relationship Concerns
- Work Stressors
- Life Stressors
- Trauma
- EAS/PCS and Challenges Related to Transition
- Grief and Loss
- Sadness
- Worry
- Deployment Cycle Stressors and Reintegration
- Adjustment
- Crisis Intervention
- Sleep Hygiene
- Parent-Child Communication

## Marine Corps Family Team Building
Enhancing the resilience, readiness, and well-being of our military community.

[Marine Corps Family Team Building](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/military-family-life/marine-corps-family-team-building) (MCFTB) is designed to enhance the resilience, readiness, and well-being of all members of the Marine Corps community, including service members, spouses, children, extended family members, command leaders, units, and support personnel.

How to get started with MCFTB:

- Identify Individual Needs
  Determine what specific support or resources you or your family require. MCFTB offers a variety of workshops, classes, and resources tailored to different needs, including deployment support, spouse education and career assistance, relationship-enhancement, and more.

  MCFTB professionals can help you identify your specific needs.

- Connect with MCFTB
  Reach out to MCFTB professionals either in person or by phone. They can provide guidance on available programs, workshops, and resources that best suit your needs.

- Attend Workshops and Classes
  Participate in MCFTB workshops, classes, and events relevant to your situation. These could include pre-deployment briefs, relationship-enhancement classes, pre-marital and marital workshops, relocation assistance workshops, family readiness seminars, financial planning classes, and more.

- Connect with Other Families
  Take advantage of opportunities to connect with other Marine Corps families through MCFTB-sponsored events, support groups, and social media platforms. Building connections with other families can provide valuable support and camaraderie.

## Libraries
Discovering resources that provide access to knowledge, innovation, and creativity.

The [Library](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/libraries) is a great resource for families and school-age children, offering books, educational programs, and activities that support learning and growth. Whether you're looking for homework help, fun storytimes, or a quiet place to read and explore, the Library provides a welcoming space for children to develop their love of learning. Stop by and discover all the ways we support your family!

**Life Skills Development Resources:**

- **Children's Collection:** A diverse selection of picture books, chapter books, movies, and audiobooks designed for young readers.

- **Summer Reading Program:** Featuring free activities and incentives to encourage a love of reading during the summer months.

- **Storytime Kits:** Themed kits that include books and activities, allowing families to enjoy storytime at their convenience.

- **Educational Programs and Activities:** Various events and workshops that enrich your children's learning experiences.

- **Access to Digital Resources:** Online materials, including e-books and educational databases, to support learning and exploration. Visit the [DoD MWR Virtual Library](https://marines.dodmwrlibraries.org/).

## Exceptional Family Members
Supporting military families with special needs and ensure availability of care.

The [Exceptional Family Member Program](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/military-family-life/exceptional-family-member-program) (EFMP) is dedicated to supporting military families by ensuring they have access to the resources and services needed to thrive. We understand that navigating military life with a family member who has special needs can be challenging, which is why EFMP works closely with the School Liaison Program to provide seamless support for educational transitions, school advocacy, and special education resources. Together, we help families find the best-fit schools, understand their rights, and access individualized services that promote academic success and overall well-being.

How EFMP Supports Families:

- **Lending Library** – Borrow sensory tools, assistive devices, and educational materials to support learning and development at home.

- **Respite Care Services** – Provides temporary relief for caregivers, ensuring they have time to recharge while their loved one receives quality care.

- **Assignment Coordination** – Ensures that families are stationed at locations with appropriate medical and educational services for their exceptional family members.

- **Advocacy & Support** – Assists families in navigating the special education system, including IEPs (Individualized Education Programs).

- **Workshops & Resources** – Offers educational sessions on topics like navigating the EFMP process, advocacy skills, and community resources.

By working together, EFMP and the School Liaison help ensure that your child receives the support they need—at home, in school, and throughout their military journey. We are here to support you every step of the way!

## Budgeting Your Child Care
Learning how to save and manage expenses.

The professionals at [Personal Financial Management](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/personal-financial-management) can help you prepare for financial changes by offering guidance on budgeting, saving, and managing educational expenses.

**Life Skills Development Resources:**

- Blended Retirement System (BRS)
- Car Buying
- Consumer Awareness
- Continuation Pay
- Couple Financial Counseling
- Credit Report and Credit Score Analysis Saving and Investing
- Credit / Debt Management
- Developing a Spending Plan
- Financial Education Action Points (FEAP)
- Individual Financial Counseling
- Major Purchases
- Military Pay & Benefits
- Retirement Planning
- Survivor Benefits Plan
- Thrift Savings Plan
- Understanding Military Retirement Benefits

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)
### Who is eligible for School Age Care?

Children ages 5-12 who are enrolled in kindergarten through 6th grade are eligible.

### How do I register my child for care?

Register online at [MilitaryChildCare.com](https://www.militarychildcare.com) and follow the steps to request care.

### Is there a waitlist for School Age Care?

Yes, if no spots are available, your child will be placed on a waitlist, and you will be notified when a spot opens.

### What are the program hours?

Hours vary by location but typically include before and after school care, full-day care on school breaks, and summer camp.

### Does School Age Care provide meals?

Breakfast and snacks are provided on school days; lunch may be required on certain days, such as teacher workdays or school breaks.

Address: 3312 Purvis Rd, Quantico, VA 22134

# School Liaison

We support military families by prioritizing the educational needs of their children, providing resources, and ensuring smooth transitions between schools.

## Connect with a School Liaison
Getting connected is easy.

## Eligibility
Members of our military community with school-aged children (PreK-12) are eligible to access the services provided by the School Liaison Program.

* Active-duty Service Members
* DoD Civilian
* National Guard
* Reserves
* Retirees

## Getting Started
Figuring out schools during a move or facing school-related questions can be tough, but you don't have to do it alone. Your School Liaison is here to help make things smoother for you and your family.

**Contact the School Liaison**
Reach out to your local School Liaison office for personalized support.

**Schedule a Consultation**
Set up a meeting or phone call with the School Liaison to discuss your child's needs, school options, and any concerns you may have regarding the transition.

**Collect Important Documents**
Maintain important records, such as school transcripts, report cards, individual education plans (IEPs), and any other documentation that will assist the School Liaison in supporting your family.

**Learn About Local School Options**
The School Liaison can provide details on the local school districts, private schools, charter schools, homeschooling, and other alternative education options to help you make an informed decision.

**Explore Available Resources**
The School Liaison can direct you to resources such as tutoring services, scholoarships, extracurricular activities, and other programs.

**Stay Connected**
Maintain communication with the School Liaison throughout your assignment to receive ongoing support and updates on educational opportunities for your child.

Don't hesitate to contact your School Liaison, who is ready to support your family's educational journey!

## School Liaisons
School Liaison Officers help to navigate the challenges of school transitions, ensuring access to quality education, and providing valuable support for your children's academic success.

Connect with a School Liaison Officer in your area.

## Our Support
The School Liaison will provide you with important information, assist with enrollment, navigate grade and credit transfers, and ensure that your child receives support to connect to their new environment. The School Liaison can also help you facilitate communication with principals, teachers, or other school staff, making your child's transition smoother.

Empowering you with the information you need, they ensure you can make informed decisions about your child's education and be their strongest advocate.

Your School Liaison is the critical link between families, commands, communities, and schools.

* Promotes and enhances education services and programs.
* Provides incoming families with information regarding Local Education Agencies.
* Leverage the Interstate Compact and assist with grade/credit transferability.
* Ensure children/youth and LEAs are supported by military community.
* Facilitate command sponsored Adopt-a-School opportunities.

## Resources for Military Families
Additional services to strengthen and support military families.

## Adjusting to Changes
Moving to a new duty station can be challenging for military families, especially for children adjusting to a new school and environment.

[Community Counseling](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/prevention-and-counseling/community-counseling) provides support to ease this transition by offering emotional support, stress management strategies, and adjustment counseling. Counselors help families navigate the challenges of relocation, offering guidance on coping with change, building resilience, and connecting with local resources.

Through individual and family counseling, the program helps create a smooth transition, strengthening the overall well-being of military families.

Life Skills Development Resources:

* Relationship Concerns
* Work Stressors
* Life Stressors
* Trauma
* EAS/PCS and Challenges Related to Transition
* Grief and Loss
* Sadness
* Worry
* Deployment Cycle Stressors and Reintegration
* Adjustment
* Crisis Intervention
* Sleep Hygiene
* Parent-Child Communication

## Budgeting for Your Move
[Personal Financial Management](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/personal-financial-management) is here to support your military family during your move to another duty station. From budgeting for relocation expenses to understanding allowances, and managing housing costs, our experts provide guidance to help you stay financially secure throughout your transition. Connect with us to plan ahead and make your move easier!

**Life Skills Development Resources:**

* Blended Retirement System (BRS)
* Car Buying
* Consumer Awareness
* Continuation Pay
* Couple Financial Counseling
* Credit Report and Credit Score Analysis Saving and Investing
* Credit / Debt Management
* Developing a Spending Plan
* Financial Education Action Points (FEAP)
* Individual Financial Counseling
* Major Purchases
* Military Pay & Benefits
* Retirement Planning
* Survivor Benefits Plan
* Thrift Savings Plan
* Understanding Military Retirement Benefits

## Libraries
The [Library](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/libraries) is a great resource for families and school-age children, offering books, educational programs, and activities that support learning and growth. Whether you're looking for homework help, fun storytimes, or a quiet place to read and explore, the Library provides a welcoming space for children to develop their love of learning. Stop by and discover all the ways we support your family!

**Life Skills Development Resources:**

* **Children's Collection:** A diverse selection of picture books, chapter books, movies, and audiobooks designed for young readers.
* **Summer Reading Program:** Featuring free activities and incentives to encourage a love of reading during the summer months.
* **Storytime Kits:** Themed kits that include books and activities, allowing families to enjoy storytime at their convenience.
* **Educational Programs and Activities:** Various events and workshops that enrich your children's learning experiences.
* **Access to Digital Resources:** Online materials, including e-books and educational databases, to support learning and exploration. Vist the [DoD MWR Virtual Library](https://marines.dodmwrlibraries.org./).

## Before & After School Care
[School Age Care](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/child-and-youth/school-age-care) (SAC) programs support your military family with after-school care, learning opportunities in a safe environment. Whether you need care before or after school, help with homework, or a nurturing home environment for your child, these programs provide safe and reliable options.

**School Age Care (SAC)**
SAC offers child care for kids in kindergarten through age 12, giving them a structured and fun environment when they're not in school. You can rely on SAC for:

* **After-School Support** – Your child will have a safe place to go before and after school, during holidays, and over the summer. They'll enjoy fun activities, make friends, and stay active while you focus on your work or military duties.
* **Educational Services** – SAC provides homework help, tutoring, and learning activities that support what your child is doing in school.
* **Support for Military Families** – If your schedule changes due to training or deployment, SAC offers flexible hours so your child always has consistent care.

Register for School Age Care at [MilitaryChildCare.com](https://public.militarychildcare.csd.disa.mil/mcc-central/mcchome#/).

## Exceptional Family Members
The [Exceptional Family Member Program](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/military-family-life/exceptional-family-member-program) (EFMP) is dedicated to supporting military families by ensuring they have access to the resources and services needed to thrive. We understand that navigating military life with a family member who has special needs can be challenging, which is why EFMP works closely with the School Liaison Program to provide seamless support for educational transitions, school advocacy, and special education resources. Together, we help families find the best-fit schools, understand their rights, and access individualized services that promote academic success and overall well-being.

How EFMP Supports Families:

* **Lending Library** – Borrow sensory tools, assistive devices, and educational materials to support learning and development at home.
* **Respite Care Services** – Provides temporary relief for caregivers, ensuring they have time to recharge while their loved one receives quality care.
* **Assignment Coordination** – Ensures that families are stationed at locations with appropriate medical and educational services for their exceptional family members.
* **Advocacy & Support** – Assists families in navigating the special education system, including IEPs (Individualized Education Programs) .
* **Workshops & Resources** – Offers educational sessions on topics like navigating the EFMP process, advocacy skills, and community resources.

By working together, EFMP and the School Liaison help ensure that your child receives the support they need—at home, in school, and throughout their military journey. We are here to support you every step of the way!

## Family Child Care
[Family Child Care](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/child-and-youth/family-child-care) (FCC) gives you in-home child care from trained and certified providers, often military spouses, in military housing. This program is great if you prefer a smaller, home-like setting for your child. FCC offers:

* **Home-Based Care** – Your child will be cared for in a safe, nurturing home setting with small group sizes and personalized attention.
* **Educational Activities** – FCC providers include age-appropriate learning, playtime, and rest in their daily schedules, helping your child grow and develop.
* **Flexible Child Care** – Whether you need full-time, part-time, or overnight care, FCC providers can work with your schedule, making it easier to handle deployments or unpredictable work hours.

## Information, Referral, and Relocation
Moving to a new duty station can be overwhelming, but you don't have to navigate it alone. [Information, Referral, and Relocation](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/information-referral-and-relocation) (IR&R) services are here to help you and your family transition smoothly and feel at home in your new community.

**Here's how IR&R can support you:**

* **Relocation Assistance** – Get guidance on housing, base services, child care, and community resources to establish stability for your family.
* **Local School Information** – Connect you to the School Liaison, educational resources, enrollment requirements, and district policies to ensure a smooth school transition.
* **Welcome Aboard Resources** – Access newcomer checklists, area guides, and personalized referrals to help you get familiar with your new surroundings.
* **Lending Locker** – Borrow temporary household items to make settling in easier while you wait for your belongings to arrive.

Wherever your journey takes you, IR&R is here to provide the information and resources you need to make your transition as smooth as possible.

## Marine Corps Family Team Building
[Marine Corps Family Team Building (MCFTB)](https://www.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/military-family-life/marine-corps-family-team-building) is designed to enhance the resilience, readiness, and well-being of all members of the Marine Corps community, including service members, spouses, children, extended family members, command leaders, units, and support personnel.

How to get started with MCFTB:

1. Identify Individual Needs: Determine what specific support or resources you or your family require. MCFTB offers a variety of workshops, classes, and resources tailored to different needs, including deployment support, spouse education and career assistance, relationship-enhancement, and more.
   
   MCFTB professionals can help you identify your specific needs.
   
2. Connect with MCFTB: Reach out to MCFTB professionals either in person or by phone. They can provide guidance on available programs, workshops, and resources that best suit your needs.
   
3. Attend Workshops and Classes: Participate in MCFTB workshops, classes, and events relevant to your situation. These could include pre-deployment briefs, relationship-enhancement classes, pre-marital and marital workshops, relocation assistance workshops, family readiness seminars, financial planning classes, and more.
   
4. Connect with Other Families: Take advantage of opportunities to connect with other Marine Corps families through MCFTB-sponsored events, support groups, and social media platforms. Building connections with other families can provide valuable support and camaraderie.

## FAQs
Find information and get quick answers to common questions.

## What does the School Liaison do?
The program helps military families navigate the education system and assists with school transitions, special education services, and local school information.

## Who can use the School Liaison?
The program is available to active-duty military families, National Guard and Reserve members on active orders, DoD civilians, and retired service members with school-aged children, whether families live on or off base.

## How can the School Liaison help during a PCS move?
School Liaisons provide resources for enrolling in new schools, transferring credits, and ensuring a smooth transition. They can also help find information on local schools, extracurricular activities, and educational support.

## What educational resources are available through the School Liaison?
School Liaisons provide access to resources such as tutoring, special education information, and connections to homeschooling or virtual school options.

## Can the School Liaison assist with special education needs?
Yes, School Liaisons can help families understand the special education process, connect with local resources, and support children with IEPs (Individualized Education Programs) or 504 Plans.

## Can School Liaisons help with college readiness?
Yes, School Liaisons provide resources for college planning, scholarships, and navigating the college admissions process.

## Do School Liaisons only work with DoDEA schools?
No, School Liaisons support families regardless of whether their children attend public, private, DoDEA schools, or homeschool families. They are knowledgeable about all education options available in the local area.
